jp-012-P01.name: Kamakura Great Buddha bronze panorama
jp-012-P01.description: Shoot the full bronze seated figure from the courtyard inside the main gate: low-angle raking light just after opening brings out the relief of the 13.35 m bronze surface; shootable all day, avoid high noon.

jp-012-P02.name: Great Buddha autumn foliage
jp-012-P02.description: From late November into early December, the maple and ginkgo behind the Great Buddha set the bronze seated figure in its most famous seasonal frame; shoot statue and foliage together from the rear of the grounds.

jp-013-P01.name: Lake Suwa sunset from Tateishi Park
jp-013-P01.description: 立石公園・諏訪湖夕景 (V1 best time: 日落前後／暮色（景點當地時間／JST）; V1 season: 全年；季節景觀另作加分，不保證當下色況 V1 migration skeleton; content to be refined in round 2.)

jp-014-P01.name: Todoroki Valley stream in soft light
jp-014-P01.description: Shoot the Yazawa stream and its green walls from the valley boardwalk: the gorge bottom wants soft light - full overcast (total cloud ≥70%) gives silky water and the richest greens.

jp-014-P02.name: Todoroki Valley autumn foliage
jp-014-P02.description: Both gorge walls along the ~600 m boardwalk turn red and the leaves ride the stream down the Yazawa - the only gorge foliage inside Tokyo's 23 wards.

jp-015-P01.name: Nijubashi moat reflection
jp-015-P01.description: From the Kokyo Gaien plaza in front of the Seimon Stone Bridge, frame the double bridge (stone bridge, iron bridge, Fushimi-yagura) with its mirror in the inner moat: a windless early morning gives the complete reflection of stonework and both bridges.

jp-015-P02.name: Kokyo Gaien plaza panorama
jp-015-P02.description: From the center of the Kokyo Gaien plaza, frame the white gravel field, black pines and the Fushimi-yagura skyline beyond; broken cloud on a fair day gives the panorama its best rhythm.

jp-016-P02.name: Yamashita Park: Yokohama Port night lights on the water
jp-016-P02.description: 山下公園・橫濱港夜景與水面光影 (V1 best time: 藍調時刻至夜間（景點當地時間／JST）; V1 season: 全年 V1 migration skeleton; content to be refined in round 2.)

jp-017-P01.name: Kenrokuen yukitsuri snow scene
jp-017-P01.description: From mid-December to late February, the yukitsuri ropes over the Karasaki pine and the Kotoji lantern are Kenrokuen's signature winter scene; on snowy days the whole garden turns white and the Kasumiga-ike reflection is at its best.

jp-017-P02.name: Morning Light Reflection at Kasumiga-ike
jp-017-P02.description: Water reflection of Kasumiga-ike and Kotoji lantern: During the early-morning opening (November 1st to end of February, 6:00–7:45, free admission), the water is calm and there are few people, making it the cleanest window for reflections in the garden. In seasons without early-morning opening, focus on the early morning after the garden opens.

jp-018-P01.name: Nagoya Castle keep panorama
jp-018-P01.description: From the Honmaru plaza, frame the Nagoya Castle great keep (5 stories, roof top 55.6 m) with its golden shachihoko: shootable all day but avoid high noon - raking dawn/dusk light gives the stone base and white walls their relief.

jp-018-P02.name: Nagoya Castle night illumination
jp-018-P02.description: The Nagoya Castle keep exterior is lit every night from sunset until 23:00 (official FAQ) and the golden keep reads against the night sky from around the closed grounds; this contract judges by the night window - the grounds themselves are not open at night, so shoot from outside.

jp-036-P03.description: 高千穗峽・划船視角真名井瀑布 (V1 best time: 僅官方當日確認租船營運且預約／現場條件允許時; V1 season: 全年；每日營運狀態由官方提供，不可由天氣推定 V1 migration skeleton; content to be refined in round 2.)

jp-037-P01.name: Unkai Terrace cloud sea
jp-037-P01.description: Cloud-sea terrace at the TOMAMU gondola top station (1,088 m): 2026 summer gondola runs 2026-05-13 to 2026-10-13 (approx. 04:30-08:00, dates shift yearly), with roughly 40% cloud-sea odds in season; the terrace switches to rime-ice operation in winter.

jp-037-P02.name: TOMAMU dawn (gondola hours)
jp-037-P02.description: Dawn on the summit during operating hours (approx. 04:30-08:00): sunrise light over ridgelines, often with the cloud deck below.

jp-038-P01.name: Zao juhyo (snow monster) plain
jp-038-P01.description: Japan's most famous snow monsters around the Zao Ropeway Jizosancho station; formation season late Dec to early Mar (peak late Jan-late Feb, official calendar).

jp-038-P02.name: Zao juhyo night illumination
jp-038-P02.description: Night-time juhyo illumination (announced yearly, approx. late Dec-late Feb 17:00-21:00); paid facility, cancelled in severe weather.

jp-039-P01.name: Kussharo cloud sea from Tsubetsu Pass
jp-039-P01.description: The highest of the three passes (947 m): when a cloud sea forms, the other passes sit inside it while this one is above it. Season Jun-Oct at dawn; road 588 is closed in winter (Nov-May).

jp-040-P01.name: Kussharo caldera panorama and cloud sea (Bihoro Pass)
jp-040-P01.description: Overlooks Japan's largest caldera lake (Kussharo) from 525 m; cloud sea in spring/autumn pre-dawn (Aug encounter rate ~38.8% 04:00-07:00); blizzard closures in winter.

jp-041-P01.name: Shiretoko drift ice onshore (Puyuni Cape)
jp-041-P01.description: Lowest-latitude drift-ice viewpoint in the northern hemisphere (World Heritage); Puyuni Cape is the classic dawn vantage. Ice onshore depends on wind/sea state and no sea-ice data source exists in the system, so this subject is honestly not_evaluatable (fail-closed); the seasonal window (late Jan-Mar) is reference only.

jp-041-P02.name: Puyuni Cape dawn
jp-041-P02.description: Sunrise over the Sea of Okhotsk horizon (east-facing vantage); icy sea cliffs in winter demand caution.

jp-042-P01.name: Moriyoshi juhyo plain
jp-042-P01.description: One of Japan's three great snow-monster sites (quiet alternative); juhyo loop about 30 min on foot from the gondola top station. Viewing period Jan 7 - Mar 5 (2025 example).

jp-042-P02.name: Juhyo under the stars (night tour)
jp-042-P02.description: Night tour (reservation required) pairing snow monsters with the night sky; clear winter nights are dark-sky class.

jp-043-P01.name: Lavender East fields
jp-043-P01.description: Japan's largest-class lavender field against the Tokachi-dake range; bloom driven by temperature and trackable in the farm's official journal; open only around Jun 20 - Jul 20 (2026 example).

jp-044-P01.name: Aoike cobalt blue
jp-044-P01.description: Spring-fed pond under the beech forest of World Heritage Shirakami; clearest blue in fine weather around 10:00-12:00 from the NW-side deck (sun azimuth dependent) - overcast/rain dulls the blue, which is exactly the model's deciding factor. On calm days the still water mirrors the forest.

jp-045-P01.name: Cape Chikyu sunset
jp-045-P01.description: A 100 m cliff over the circular Pacific horizon (Muroran's finest view); the lighthouse sits on the north side, sunset works the western face; parking became paid in April 2026.

jp-045-P02.name: Circular Pacific horizon overlook
jp-045-P02.description: Open 24h; winter brings less sea fog and better transparency (horizon lines); the core criterion is air clarity.

jp-046-P01.name: Phantom bridge reflection
jp-046-P01.description: 1937 eleven-arch bridge of the old JNR Shihoro line; Nukabira lake level decides how much shows (roughly visible Jan frozen lake to mid-May); calm-dawn reflections decide the shot; lake-walking needs guided winter tours.

jp-047-P01.name: Hakkoda snow monsters
jp-047-P01.description: One of Japan's three great snow-monster sites (Aomori); the 1,324 m summit is whiteout-prone; ropeway winter hours 09:00-15:40 (Dec-Feb), suspended over ~25 m/s winds.

jp-048-P01.name: Kitayamazaki cliff panorama
jp-048-P01.description: 200 m cliffs running ~8 km - the 'Alps of the sea', rated Special-A (the only coastal one nationally); summer yamase sea fog governs visibility, which the model can judge; 736 steps to the main decks.

jp-048-P02.name: Kitayamazaki dawn
jp-048-P02.description: East-facing cliffs put the sunrise dead-centre in the frame; winter NE blizzards make the stairways hazardous.

jp-049-P01.name: Okama five-colour crater lake
jp-049-P01.description: A ~1,600 m-class crater lake, emerald-green and strongly acidic; its hue shifts with the sun angle - direction and cloud cover are model-judgeable; a live webcam (late Apr-early Nov) provides verification; the eco/hyline roads close Nov-Apr.

jp-051-P01.name: Itsukushima torii in the sea (high tide)
jp-051-P01.description: The famous torii stands in the sea at high tide; at low tide the base can be approached. Shrine buildings and sea reflections work year-round.

jp-052-P01.name: Bitchu Matsuyama Castle in a sea of clouds
jp-052-P01.description: Japan's only surviving castle keep on a mountain: the cloud-sea lookout frames the tenshu over ridgelines, dawn only, late Sep-early Apr (strongest late Oct-early Dec, per Takahashi City).

jp-053-P01.name: Amanohashidate panoramic view (Nihon Sankei)
jp-053-P01.description: One of Japan's three famous views: the pine-lined sandbar seen from the overlooks (Kasamatsu Park / Amanohashidate View Land) across Miyazu Bay.

jp-054-P01.name: Ine Bay funaya skyline on calm water
jp-054-P01.description: 230 boathouses line the bay; at calm mornings the waterfront skyline reflects on the sea, sometimes with harbour mist.

jp-055-P01.name: Tottori dunes wind-rippled sunset
jp-055-P01.description: Japan's largest coastal dunes: low-angle evening light sculpts wind ripples and dune shadows; clear ripples after wind-blown dusting are the key.

jp-056-P01.name: Daisen summit view over the Sea of Japan
jp-056-P01.description: Highest peak of the Chugoku region (1,729 m): the summit looks over the forested slopes to the Sea of Japan; winter snow closes or hardens the trail.

jp-057-P01.name: Nagasaki's ten-million-dollar night view from Mt. Inasa
jp-057-P01.description: One of Japan's three great night views: the 333 m summit observatory over Nagasaki harbour and the hillside city lights.

jp-058-P01.name: Active Sakurajima: Minami-dake crater view
jp-058-P01.description: From the Yunohira observatory (~373 m, closest public viewpoint to the active crater): Minami-dake plumes over Kinko Bay; alert levels follow JMA notices.

jp-059-P01.name: Aso Kusasenri grassland with volcanic skyline
jp-059-P01.description: Grassland (about 25 km2) on the double caldera: grazing horses against the steaming Nakadake crater; when the crater road is closed, the grassland view still stands.

jp-060-P01.name: Tsunoshima Bridge arc over Amase-seto
jp-060-P01.description: The 1,780 m island bridge curves across the emerald Amase-seto channel inside Kita-Nagato Kaigan Quasi-National Park.

jp-061-P01.name: Kintaikyo's five wooden arches on the Nishiki River
jp-061-P01.description: Five wooden arches (rebuilt by craft every 3 years since 1673) mirrored in the Nishiki River, best with autumn colour or early-summer green.

jp-062-P01.name: Vine bridge over the deep Iya gorge
jp-062-P01.description: One of Japan's three odd bridges (folk-art monument): a 45 m vine bridge over the V-shaped Iya gorge; crossing 08:00-18:00, occasional winter-snow closures; nightly illumination 19:00-21:30 (no crossing).

jp-063-P01.name: Matsuyama Castle keep and Inland Sea view
jp-063-P01.description: The surviving keep on Katsuyama hill (first built 1608) looks over Matsuyama city and the Seto Inland Sea; ropeway hours follow on-site notices.

jp-064-P01.name: Motonosumi's 123 vermilion torii on the sea cliff
jp-064-P01.description: 123 vermilion torii climb the sea cliff toward the Sea of Japan; the red line against blue water is the subject in any light.

jp-065-P01.name: Mount Fuji summit at Kengamine
jp-065-P01.description: From Japan's highest summit Kengamine: cloud sea, sunrise gonore, shadow Fuji (ja.wikipedia; open hiking season per official notices); subject-disjoint from jp-066 Chureito 4.8 km (hillside pagoda classic).

jp-065-P02.name: Sunset alpenglow on Mt. Fuji summit
jp-065-P02.description: The warm band just after sunset lights the Kengamine snow face (snow season only): from the summit viewpoint the crater rim turns gold then red at sunset - the Japanese 'Mackinaw' (yamagai) phenomenon; a clear summit and sightline are required.

jp-065-P03.name: Snow scene on Mt. Fuji summit
jp-065-P03.description: Mt. Fuji summit (Kengamine) in snow season: snow on the crater rim and Kengamine, snow cornices on the hut row - qualifies inside the snow-season window (snow line above the 5th station) with ground snow, temp <= 1 C, visibility >= 3 km.

jp-066-P01.name: Chureito Pagoda with Mount Fuji
jp-066-P01.description: The classic pagoda-and-Fuji composition from the hillside deck (ja.wikipedia); disjoint from the jp-065 summit climb and the existing lakeside Fuji spot.

jp-067-P01.name: Taisho Pond Yakedake reflection
jp-067-P01.description: Standing dead trees and mirrored Yakedake from the 1915 eruption-formed pond (ja.wikipedia); subject-disjoint from Shinhotaka ropeway summit 3.8 km (panorama) - reflection subject is not expressible by that neighbour's templates.

jp-068-P01.name: Mikuri-ga-ike Tateyama range reflection
jp-068-P01.description: High-altitude pond mirroring the Tateyama range at Murodo (access-season only; winter closure); kin to jp-067 Taisho Pond but alpine lake vs valley dead-trees.

jp-068-P02.name: Yuki-no-Otani snow corridor
jp-068-P02.description: Up to ~16-20 m snow walls by the Murodo bus stop (official Alpine Route; April opening to end-May); contract uses OUR snow-state/visibility semantics re-derived, not copied prose.

jp-069-P01.name: Biei patchwork hills and famous trees
jp-069-P01.description: Rolling farmland patchwork with solitary trees such as the Ken & Mary tree (ja.wikipedia); disjoint landform from jp-001 Blue Pond 17.6 km.

jp-070-P01.name: Oirase stream-walk cascade
jp-070-P01.description: A 14 km stream-walk with cascades including Ashura Falls (ja.wikipedia); conditions re-derived in our flow/mist/visibility semantics.

jp-071-P01.name: Tsubo-numa dawn-glow reflection
jp-071-P01.description: The pond fires only when three conditions coincide - civil light (sun elevation > -6 deg), windless still water, and peak foliage (short late-Oct window, local tourism source); re-derived in OUR semantics: reflection = still-water contract, calendar window 10/15-10/31 is the typical foliage peak, not a guarantee.

jp-072-P01.name: Gassho village winter light-up
jp-072-P01.description: Winter illumination over the gassho farmhouses (official light-up page, yearly announced mid-Jan to late Feb, shuttle-only access); an artificial-light night subject - daytime hours never qualify. UNESCO World Heritage.

jp-073-P01.name: SORA terrace summit cloud sea
jp-073-P01.description: SORA terrace at 1,933 m over Shinshu morning clouds (official; within the gondola season, best around sunrise) - cloud-sea verdict by the LCL = DEM-200 formula (1,733 m), not marketing prose.

jp-074-P01.name: Takeda Castle in the cloud sea
jp-074-P01.description: Deep-autumn mornings when valley radiation fog fills the basin and the castle floats (Takeda city official); verdict follows the LCL formula - keep base 353.6 m gives LCL 153.6 m, requiring an extremely low inversion cloud top; never a daily guarantee.

jp-075-P01.name: Chichibu basin fog sea
jp-075-P01.description: From the summit deck the basin's radiation fog becomes a sea on clear cold mornings (ja.wikipedia); disjoint from jp-074 Takeda (castle-body subject) - here the pure basin fog sea.

jp-076-P01.name: Daikanbo over the Aso five peaks
jp-076-P01.description: From the outer-rim ridge the five caldera peaks and Kusasenri grassland unfold (ja.wikipedia); subject-disjoint from Mt Aso Kusasenri 3.6 km (grassland ground-level) - here the rim overlook.

jp-077-P01.name: Lake torii at sunset
jp-077-P01.description: The torii standing in Lake Biwa with sunset behind (ja.wikipedia); disjoint from the existing Kyoto spots 39+ km.

jp-078-P01.name: Fumotohama mirror beach
jp-078-P01.description: The governing condition is the tide (spring-tide low-water + calm), not weather; the system has no tide data source, so the contract is honestly not_evaluatable (fail-closed, CL-DATA-20 tidal semantics); informational note Mar-Nov spring-tide clear evenings.

jp-079-P01.name: Goshiki-numa cobalt water
jp-079-P01.description: Volcanic ponds whose water shifts cobalt-to-emerald with sky and depth (ja.wikipedia; winter closure, open Apr-Nov); disjoint from jp-071 Tsubo-numa (dawn-glow reflection) - here the water colour itself.

jp-080-P01.name: Diamond Fuji sunrise over Lake Tanuki
jp-080-P01.description: On mid-April dawns the rising sun sits on Fuji's summit as seen from the lake - Diamond Fuji (Fuji city official; spring window 4/10-4/25, with a second late-August window noted in the rationale); the lake mirror is a bonus, not required.

jp-081-P01.name: Nabegataki behind-the-fall corridor
jp-081-P01.description: The representative behind-the-fall viewpoint (ja.wikipedia; paid park entry 9:00-17:00 per current notices); disjoint from the rim-overlook Aso spots and the grassland.

jp-082-P01.name: Niyodo Blue water
jp-082-P01.description: Japan's clearest river running gemstone blue in its upper reaches (ja.wikipedia; 'Niyodo Blue' has no single authoritative point - this is an honest village-anchor pending field survey); disjoint from volcanic-lake colour jp-079.

jp-083-P01.name: Fukiware Falls sea-splitting cascade
jp-083-P01.description: The Tone tributary tears across a 30 m rock shelf 'like a sea split open' (ja.wikipedia); disjoint from jp-070 Oirase (multi-cascade stream-walk) - here one massive waterfall body.

jp-084-P01.name: Candle Rock sunset ignition
jp-084-P01.description: When the setting sun aligns on the 20 m rock's tip it looks lit like a candle (Japan NTO official; only calm clear days and by excursion boat - boats run 3/15-11/30 by reservation, the seasonal window tracks the operating period); the Ojirobana Park deck is the land fallback.

jp-085-P01.name: Devil's Washboard strata
jp-085-P01.description: Recessional ripple-sandstone shelves ringing the islet (ja.wikipedia; best at low tide - no tide data source, so visibility is an informational note and the contract never fabricates a reverse threshold, re-derived in our landform semantics); disjoint from inland rim jp-076.

jp-086-P01.name: Kujukushima islet seascape
jp-086-P01.description: 208 islets across a rias coast, seen from Tenkai-ho / Ishidake decks (Sasebo official); disjoint from single-rock sunset jp-084 - here the archipelago topology.

jp-087-P01.name: Nemophila blue sea
jp-087-P01.description: 4.5 million nemophila over Miharashi hill beside the sea (park official, late Apr-mid May, dates yearly announced); disjoint from farm-patchwork jp-069.

jp-087-P02.name: Kochia crimson spheres
jp-087-P02.description: Kochia turn crimson through October (park official); same park as P01 but a different season.

jp-088-P01.name: Tea-terrace Fuji panorama
jp-088-P01.description: One of the very few wire-free tea-field Fuji compositions (Fuji city official; tea-picking Apr-May is the fresh-bud season but the subject is shootable year-round - the season is informational, never a hard gate); disjoint from jp-080 Lake Tanuki (Diamond Fuji sunrise).

jp-089-P01.name: Achi Village Milky Way night
jp-089-P01.description: Rated Japan's clearest skies by the MoE national survey (ja.wikipedia; the 4-9月 stargazing programmes are operating plans while the star-sky contract holds year-round); geographically disjoint from existing Hokkaido/Tohoku night-sky spots.

jp-090-P01.name: Southern Cross over the night sea
jp-090-P01.description: The only inhabited Japanese island where the full Southern Cross is visible (ja.wikipedia; Dec-Jun is the observation season - a season-window condition governs whether the subject qualifies, the sky-condition contract is evaluated only inside the season); Japan's southernmost inhabited island.

jp-091-P01.name: Mossy ravine stream mist
jp-091-P01.description: A granite-boulder ravine with moss-draped sugi forest on a World Natural Heritage island (ja.wikipedia; the 'Mononoke forest'); disjoint from jp-081 Nabegataki (behind-the-fall curtain) - here moss-gorge stream atmosphere.

jp-092-P01.name: Umi Jigoku cobalt pool
jp-092-P01.description: A 98C cobalt-blue boiling pool with rising steam (ja.wikipedia; nationally designated Place of Scenic Beauty, 2009; viewed from visitor facilities, steam peaks on cold mornings while pool color is richest under midday top-light - opposite of golden hour, recorded honestly); disjoint from the inland Kyushu onsen villages.

jp-093-P01.name: Chinoike Jigoku red pond
jp-093-P01.description: A scarlet boiling-mud pond (ja.wikipedia; same hell tour as Umi Jigoku but a red-mud color subject; midday top-light is the color optimum - honestly recorded); disjoint from inland onsen subjects.

jp-094-P01.name: Yubatake steam flumes
jp-094-P01.description: Wooden flumes pouring steaming spring water at the heart of Kusatsu (ja.wikipedia; nationally designated Special Place of Scenic Beauty; discharge is constant and not a weather contract - steam reads best on cold mornings, color richest at midday - honestly recorded); disjoint from other Gunma/Nagano subjects.

jp-095-P01.name: Jigokudani steam and macaques
jp-095-P01.description: Fissure steam and snow-bathing Japanese macaques (ja.wikipedia; wild-animal behavior is not forecastable - presence honestly marked uncertain; icy winter trail - access informational); disjoint from other Nagano subjects.

tw-001-P04.name: Datunshan: Taipei Basin city night view
tw-001-P04.description: City night view over the Taipei Basin from the platform in front of the Datunshan navigation station: light fields across the Tamsui River and downtown Taipei, with the Guanyin Mountain silhouette. A city-night subject under light-pollution conditions; visibility and total cloud cover are the main criteria, and shooting requires after civil dusk (sun <= -6 deg).

tw-002-P01.name: Taipei 101 dusk / blue hour from Xiangshan Photographers Platform
tw-002-P01.description: Shoot Taipei 101 and the Xinyi skyline at dusk and blue hour from Xiangshan. The Photographers Platform and the Six Giants Rocks are the recognized spots for framing 101; best in blue hour (sun -4 to -8 degrees after sunset).

tw-006-P01.description: Shoot the red steel arches of Guandu Bridge with the Guanyinshan river panorama from the riverside viewing towers or bank trails: aerial perspective layers the far ridge, mid-level cloud bands and low cloud control the stacking; shootable all day, best in daylight and around dawn/dusk.

tw-006-P02.name: Guandu Bridge sunset
tw-006-P02.description: Shoot the Guandu Bridge sunset around dusk: the Bali-side left-bank viewing tower faces the setting sun, catching gilded arches with the Guanyinshan silhouette; sunset window +/-40 minutes.

tw-006-P03.name: Guandu Bridge night illumination and light trails
tw-006-P03.description: Shoot the Guandu Bridge night illumination and light trails: the flood-lit arches and traffic light trails are the subject, requiring civil darkness, high visibility and low cloud; daytime hours never qualify.

tw-007-P01.name: Bitan suspension bridge twilight illumination and water reflection
tw-007-P01.description: Shoot the Bitan suspension bridge illumination with Xindian River reflections in the blue-hour window after sunset: the sky still reads blue while the bridge lights come up; window is sun elevation -4 to -8 deg from coordinates.

tw-007-P02.name: Bitan suspension bridge night illumination and water reflection
tw-007-P02.description: Shoot the Bitan bridge night illumination reflected in the Xindian River: low wind turns the pool into a mirror for a symmetric composition of lit bridge and reflection; requires civil darkness, daytime hours never qualify.

tw-086-P01.name: Bali Kantou Danjiang Bridge Viewpoint - Danjiang Bridge half-hidden in fog
tw-086-P01.description: Photograph the Danjiang Bridge half-hidden in river-valley fog from the Bali hillside viewpoint: valley fog half-erases the bridge and the far city skyline - a subject where low visibility is exactly right. Coordinates are owner-provided (Google Maps resolved to @25.140639,121.420333); the viewpoint faces the Tamsui River and the bridge (exact bearing unverified). Adjacent to, but deliberately distinct from, the legacy on-the-bridge Danjiang Bridge subject.

tw-086-P02.name: Bali Kantou Danjiang Bridge Viewpoint - clear daytime view of Danjiang Bridge
tw-086-P02.description: A clear daytime view of the Danjiang Bridge and the Tamsui River from the Bali hillside viewpoint: with clean air (visibility >= 5 km, AOD <= 0.4) and little low cloud (<= 30%), the bridge structure and river reflections stay readable. Same owner-provided coordinate and facing as P01; adjacent to, but distinct from, the legacy Danjiang Bridge subject.

tw-086-P03.name: Bali Kantou Danjiang Bridge Viewpoint - blazing sunset clouds over Danjiang Bridge
tw-086-P03.description: At sunset the Bali hillside viewpoint frames blazing clouds above the Danjiang Bridge: low-angle backlight dyes mid/high cloud red-orange with the bridge as silhouette. "Blazing clouds" means the sunset-glow semantics. Same owner-provided coordinate and facing as P01; adjacent to, but distinct from, the legacy Danjiang Bridge subject.

tw-087-P01.name: Daxueshan 43K cloud sea
tw-087-P01.description: Forest-road access to the viewpoint lot; cloud-sea/radiation-fog season roughly Oct-Apr; the recreation area closes at night - stay inside opening hours.

tw-088-P01.name: Cuifeng Lake morning mist
tw-088-P01.description: Taiwan's largest alpine lake (1,840 m): morning mist peaks in autumn-winter; respect Taipingshan opening hours (weekday/holiday schedules differ).

tw-088-P02.name: Cuifeng Lake reflections
tw-088-P02.description: Mirror reflections from the loop-trail viewpoints on calm mornings; boardwalks are safe, stay inside park hours.

tw-088-P03.name: Cuifeng Lake loop trail in fog
tw-088-P03.description: Morning fog on the Cuifeng Lake loop trail — lake moisture meets the hemlock woods, mist drifting over the water and the trailside forest. The fog IS the subject: 50-500 m visibility along the lakeside loop; disjoint from the lake/cloud-sea subjects (this shoots fog locked over the lakeside woods).

tw-089-P01.name: Holy Ridge cloud sea (Zhenshan deck)
tw-089-P01.description: Known as the home of cloud seas - the season runs late autumn to spring; Zhenshan loop about 2h inside Shei-Pa trails; icy in winter; the Holy Ridge cloud sea is the subject (Dabajian summit is a climb, not a cloud-sea deck).

tw-089-P02.name: Guanwu Zhenshan trail in fog
tw-089-P02.description: Guanwu - the place name IS the subject. The Zhenshan trail runs through the mid-elevation cloud-belt forest, fog surging along the cypress woods and ridge. The fog IS the subject: 50-500 m visibility; disjoint from the Guanwu cloud-sea subject (this shoots the fogged forest itself).

tw-091-P01.name: Smangus cloud sea
tw-091-P01.description: Deep-mountain tribal cloud sea, late autumn to spring; the final 20 km of steep industry road makes solo night driving inadvisable.

tw-091-P02.name: Smangus night sky
tw-091-P02.description: Dark northern-mountain skies; stay overnight in the village and shoot from there rather than driving the mountain road at night.

tw-091-P03.name: Smangus fog forest
tw-091-P03.description: The cloud-belt forest of Smangus — cypress woods and giant trees around the mid-elevation village, morning fog surging up the ravines to wrap the canopy. The fog IS the subject: 50-500 m visibility; disjoint from the village/giant-tree subjects (this shoots fog through the woods).

tw-093-P01.name: Lishan valley cloud sea
tw-093-P01.description: Lishan valley cloud sea in autumn-winter; the farm gates and controls nights - do not linger in restricted areas after hours.

tw-093-P02.name: Fushoushan alpine night sky
tw-093-P02.description: Dark 2,600 m alpine skies; shoot from the lodging zone and keep clear of night-restricted areas.

tw-093-P03.name: Snow scene at Fushoushan Farm
tw-093-P03.description: Fushoushan Farm after a cold snap in snow season: snow on the tea terraces and orchard paths, the Hehuan ridgeline white in the distance - qualifies inside the snow-season window with ground snow, temp <= 1 C, visibility >= 3 km.

tw-094-P01.name: Dongju lighthouse night sky
tw-094-P01.description: Offshore-island lighthouse under dark skies; access is the hardest (ferry via Nangan/Beigan to Juguang) and sailings depend on sea state - keep a fallback; lighthouse grounds have opening-hour limits.

tw-095-P01.name: Tataka night sky
tw-095-P01.description: Galactic core over the western gateway of Yushan National Park (the existing Yushan summit record is a climb-type subject); frost on the roads at night, high-altitude cold and sambar deer on the move.

tw-095-P02.name: Couple Trees mountain vista
tw-095-P02.description: The roadside couple-tree landmark at T21 141.2K with layered Yushan ranges behind; a daylight subject under the civil light window.

tw-098-P01.name: Weishui Hill morning mist glow
tw-098-P01.description: Overlook-plane radiation fog / low cloud over the Lanyang Plain at dawn (Oct-Mar mist season); subject-disjoint from tw-031 Matcha Mountain 3.28 km away (hiking-trail mountain scenery) - this place is a plain-fog-sea overlook.

tw-098-P02.name: Weishui Hill night view
tw-098-P02.description: Night-time sea of lights across the Lanyang Plain (Yilan/Luodong) with Guishan Island on the horizon; geographically disjoint from existing night-view places.

tw-099-P01.name: Taoyuan Valley grassland sea view
tw-099-P01.description: A ~3 km rolling grass ridge above the Guishan Island sea (Northeast Coast NSC); distinct from tw-099 Caoling saddle 7.1 km (historic-trail silvergrass) and the tw-075 beach 12 km.

tw-100-P01.name: Shiding Qiandao Lake morning mist
tw-100-P01.description: Bent emerald reservoir arms and islets under morning mist (autumn-winter pre-dawn, official New Taipei tourism); disjoint from tw-018 Sun Moon Lake (grand-lake classic) and tw-098 plain-fog overlook.

tw-101-P01.name: Linkou Shuiniukeng badlands
tw-101-P01.description: Eroded red badlands running straight to the sea (zh.wikipedia); unlike inland badlands tw-027 Tianliao 27.6 km, here badlands meet the horizon line; disjoint from tw-008 Guanyinshan 8.8 km.

tw-102-P01.name: Sandiaojiao easternmost sunrise
tw-102-P01.description: First sunrise on Taiwan's easternmost cape (Maritime and Transport Bureau); geographically disjoint from tw-034 Qingshui Cliff and tw-069 Lanyu sunrises.

tw-103-P01.name: Qingjing cloud sea above the mist
tw-103-P01.description: Pasture-belt viewpoint at 1,748 m over the Hehuan range cloud sea (Nantou county official); subject-disjoint from summit-climb tw-019 Hehuan 15.3 km and tw-043 Qilai peaks.

tw-104-P01.name: Wangyou Forest drowned-cedar reflection
tw-104-P01.description: Drowned cedar snags and water reflections formed after the 1999 earthquake (Zhushan); distinct from tw-053 Sun Link Sea streams 4.3 km and the alpine-lake tw-088 Cuifeng.

tw-104-P02.name: Wangyou Forest in fog
tw-104-P02.description: The flooded-pond cedar woods of Wangyou Forest are among Taiwan's most reliable fog subjects — the marsh water lets fog form right against the trunks. The fog IS the subject: 50-500 m visibility over mirror water; disjoint from the clear-day reflection subject (this shoots fog weighing on the reflections).

tw-105-P01.name: Taiping Bridge cloud sea at dusk
tw-105-P01.description: A 1,000 m skywalk over the Jiannan plain and the 36-bend road (Alishan NSC official); related-but-distinct from tw-022 Er Yanping tea-terrace mist 17.3 km — here the bridge structure and the full bend panorama dominate.

tw-106-P01.name: Wannian Canyon water-cut marble
tw-106-P01.description: A rapidly incised tributary gorge with water-cut banded rock walls (official canyon guide site); a stream-cut landform unlike the coastal cliff tw-034.

tw-107-P01.name: Jialeshui weathered sandstone coast
tw-107-P01.description: Weathered sandstone shore platforms with sculpted rocks (Dapeng Bay NSC official); distinct from the coral-limestone lighthouse cape tw-029 and the Yehliu hoodoos tw-074.

tw-108-P01.name: Longtoushan incised meander loop
tw-108-P01.description: An incised meander hill ringed on three sides by the Zhuokou River bend (Maolin NSC official); a river-meander landform distinct from badlands tw-027 and sea-cut tw-108.

tw-109-P01.name: Qigu lagoon sunset with salt mountain
tw-109-P01.description: Oyster-rack lagoon water under sunset with the white salt mountain as foreground (Southwest Coast NSC); kin to tw-026 tile-pan salt fields 13.4 km but carries the salt-mound mass and lagoon water.

tw-110-P01.name: Sicao mangrove green tunnel
tw-110-P01.description: A 50-year native mangrove tunnel over the drainage channel behind Dazhong Temple (SW Coast NSC, by boat); distinct from forest-trail tw-084 Danongdafu and swamp-reflection tw-105 Wangyou.

tw-111-P01.name: Lotus Pond pagodas at blue hour
tw-111-P01.description: The Dragon-Tiger pagodas and Spring-Autumn pavilions reflected in the lotus pond at dusk (Tourism Bureau official); disjoint from harbor-container tw-028 Pier-2 6.9 km and Tamsui tw-003.

tw-112-P01.name: Taroko marble gorge
tw-112-P01.description: The narrowest marble gorge cut by the Liwu River (Taroko NP HQ official; trail openings follow current park notices); a canyon-floor view disjoint from sea-cliff tw-034 Qingshui 8.6 km in the same park.

tw-113-P01.name: Baiyang twin falls and water curtain
tw-113-P01.description: Twin falls and the water-curtain tunnel at the Baiyang trail end (zh.wikipedia); distinct from three-tiered tw-055 Wufengqi and the ridge tw-016.

tw-114-P01.name: Chike Mountain daylily bloom
tw-114-P01.description: Daylily seas over ~900 m farmstead ridges (zh.wikipedia: Aug-Oct); a sister to tw-035 Liushishi 6.9 km in the same bloom but with a different ridge viewpoint and the heritage farmstead landmarks.

tw-115-P01.name: Luye Highlands balloon season
tw-115-P01.description: A 350 m terrace over the Huadong Valley with tethered balloons each July-August; disjoint from tw-039 Brown Avenue fields 8 km and the coastal tw-037 station.

tw-116-P01.name: Taimali daylily sea at sunrise
tw-116-P01.description: ~110 ha of daylilies facing a Pacific sunrise (Taimali Township official; bloom ~Aug-Sep); kin to tw-115 Chike (same bloom, inland valley) but this cape faces the east coast sunrise; disjoint from tw-037 11.3 km.

tw-117-P01.name: Tongpan basalt column ring
tw-117-P01.description: The whole island is ringed by columnar basalt — 'Penghu's Yellowstone' (Penghu NSC official); kin to tw-079 Chixi falls 6.2 km (single-face columns) but here a full ring plus the lotus-seat platform.

tw-118-P01.name: Lisong emerald wild-spring pools
tw-118-P01.description: Emerald wild-spring pools against mineral-white rock in the Xinwulu tributary gorge (zh.wikipedia; 1,075 m); distinct from undersea tw-068 Zhaori and meander tw-109.

tw-119-P01.name: Jiali Mountain cloud sea and far ranges
tw-119-P01.description: A first-order triangulation summit with views to the Leshan radar ridgeline and the west coast in clear weather (Forestry Bureau trail official); disjoint from tw-089 Guanwu 15.4 km and central tw-016.

tw-120-P01.name: Wuling cherry blossom season
tw-120-P01.description: Cherry-lined farm roads at 1,740-2,200 m with the Xueshan cirque behind (Tourism Bureau blossom-season official; Feb access controlled); disjoint from cloud-sea tw-093 Fushoushan and summit-climb tw-041.

tw-120-P02.name: Snow scene at Wuling Farm
tw-120-P02.description: Wuling Farm after a cold snap in snow season: snow along the Chijiawan Creek and on the peak line (Taoshan / Snow North ridge), frosted orchards - qualifies inside the snow-season window with ground snow, temp <= 1 C, visibility >= 3 km.

tw-120-P03.name: Wuling Farm morning fog woods
tw-120-P03.description: Morning fog woods of the Qijiawan valley at Wuling Farm — radiative cooling in the cold basin forms fog along the stream bed and forest edge. The fog IS the subject: 50-500 m visibility, morning window priority; disjoint from the Wuling cherry-blossom subject (this shoots fog over the valley woods).

tw-121-P01.name: Tanghou Beach blue tears
tw-121-P01.description: Noctiluca blue-glow wave edges on Beigan's longest beach (Matsu NSB official tears-chasing spot; long exposure + high ISO; bioluminescence density is NOT forecastable - verify on site, conditions honestly marked uncertain); disjoint from the Qinbi stone-village subject.

tw-122-P01.name: Beihai Tunnel rowing blue tears
tw-122-P01.description: Rock tunnel with zero light pollution and still water; the official night rowing tour gets you to the glow up close (reservation-based, nightly 18:30-21:00, six slots - access informational; density not forecastable, verify on site); disjoint from the Iron Fort / Nangan island subjects.

tw-123-P01.name: Fuzheng Beach blue tears
tw-123-P01.description: Blue-glow wave edges on Dongju's white sand beach, an officially listed tears-chasing spot (Matsu Daily/Matsu NSB; dark at night - access informational; density not forecastable); disjoint from the Dongju Lighthouse subject.

tw-124-P01.name: Dahan stronghold coastal blue tears
tw-124-P01.description: Blue glow in breaking surf along the rocky Tieban coast (officially listed tears-chasing spot; treacherous night rocks - access informational, never go alone; density not forecastable); disjoint from Iron Fort and the tunnel's still-water subject.

tw-125-P01.name: Dalunshan tea-terrace cloud sea
tw-125-P01.description: Winter cloud sea rolling over the high-altitude tea terraces of Lugu (Nantou tourism official: the winter cloud sea is the signature); disjoint from Wuyou Forest's mirror-lake subject.

tw-125-P02.name: Dalunshan dawn over the central ranges
tw-125-P02.description: Dawn from the Guanwu pavilion overlooking five central counties; cold early mornings give the richest mist.

tw-126-P01.name: Night view over the Beishi river valley
tw-126-P01.description: Temple-front lookout over the Beishi river valley and Pinglin town lights (listed night-view spot; elevation honestly left empty - no authoritative source).

tw-127-P01.name: Xianshan cloud-mist sea
tw-127-P01.description: Xianshan is wrapped in drifting cloud-mist year round ('fairyland' wording from the official tourism open data; 967 m); disjoint from Chiali-shan's ridge-view subject.

tw-128-P01.name: Moyanshan glowing city lights (liuli)
tw-128-P01.description: Summit platform over the Miaoli city light-sea (a photographer-listed liuli-glow/night spot; 157 m).

tw-129-P01.name: Jiangziliao sunrise from the 4-way platform
tw-129-P01.description: Four viewing platforms on the summit - Pingxi peaks to the south, Wuzhi range and Keelung Isle to the north (zh.wikipedia; 729 m).

tw-129-P02.name: Jiangziliao night: Keelung Isle lights
tw-129-P02.description: On clear nights the Keelung Isle and harbor lights are visible to the north; separate from the sunrise contract.

tw-130-P01.name: Yulao cloud sea at the front/back mountain divide
tw-130-P01.description: The divide between Jianshi's front and back mountains (1,450 m); cloud seas roll over the saddle; disjoint from other Jianshi subjects.

tw-130-P02.name: Yulao night view
tw-130-P02.description: 'On clear nights an excellent night-view spot' (official Jianshi cultural-museum note); separate from the cloud-sea contract.

tw-131-P01.name: Shanshang Renjia cloud sea
tw-131-P01.description: Cloud seas surround the farm at ~1200 m (official tourism open data / UDN: cloud sea and sunrise); disjoint from other Hsinchu subjects.

tw-131-P02.name: Shanshang Renjia sunrise
tw-131-P02.description: East-facing sunrise outlook (UDN: star-gazing, cloud sea and sunrise); separate from the cloud-sea contract.

tw-132-P01.name: Ergeshan night over the Taipei basin
tw-132-P01.description: Summit platform over the Taipei basin night lights (zh.wikipedia; 678 m); disjoint from other Shiding subjects.

tw-132-P02.name: Ergeshan sunrise
tw-132-P02.description: Summit sunrise outlook; separate from the night contract.

tw-133-P01.name: Jiji Dashan night over Sun-Moon Lake
tw-133-P01.description: Summit lookout over Sun-Moon Lake and the Zhuoshui valley by night (Nantou tourism official); disjoint from lakeside subjects.

tw-133-P02.name: Jiji Dashan cloud sea

us-097-P01.name: Badlands spires at first light
us-097-P01.description: Layered erosional spires of the Badlands wall line up to the east; the striped sediments only read in low-angle light, and the dark-sky core rewards dry clear nights.

us-097-P02.name: Badlands Milky Way / star field
us-097-P02.description: Layered erosional spires of the Badlands wall line up to the east; the striped sediments only read in low-angle light, and the dark-sky core rewards dry clear nights.

us-098-P01.name: Cadillac first light above the sea fog
us-098-P01.description: The highest point on the U.S. eastern seaboard; sunrise often sits above valley fog — fog and mid-cloud decide whether the first light and the island-dotted bay appear.

us-098-P02.name: Cadillac panoramic island overlook
us-098-P02.description: The highest point on the U.S. eastern seaboard; sunrise often sits above valley fog — fog and mid-cloud decide whether the first light and the island-dotted bay appear.

us-099-P01.name: Hawksbill overlook over the Shenandoah valleys
us-099-P01.description: The park's highest observation platform; valley morning fog and visibility decide the layered-ridge panorama.

us-100-P01.name: Mono Lake tufa reflections
us-100-P01.description: Limestone tufa towers in an alkaline lake; reflections need windless water and the high-desert dark sky carries the Milky Way.

us-100-P02.name: Mono Lake Milky Way / star field
us-100-P02.description: Limestone tufa towers in an alkaline lake; reflections need windless water and the high-desert dark sky carries the Milky Way.

us-101-P01.name: Thor's Well pouring at sunset
us-101-P01.description: At higher tides the sea pours into a basalt hole like a fountain; tide, swell and low-angle sunset light jointly decide the frame.

us-102-P01.name: Multnomah Falls tiered flow
us-102-P01.description: A 620-ft tiered fall; flow varies seasonally (highest winter/spring) and the all-day subject carries a civil light window.

us-103-P01.name: Haystack Rock at sunset / sea mist
us-103-P01.description: A 235-ft sea stack facing the western horizon; low cloud/sea fog and low tide decide the silhouette and foreground reflections.

us-104-P01.name: Artists Bluff over Franconia Notch
us-104-P01.description: A bare-bluff summit over the Lafayette ridgeline and notch fog; the New England fall foliage ridge is the variable subject.

us-105-P01.name: Miners Castle lakeshore overlook
us-105-P01.description: A mineral-stained sandstone castle on Lake Superior; lake fog and low cloud decide how clearly the banded colors read.

us-106-P01.name: Santa Elena Canyon vista
us-106-P01.description: Rio Grande-carved 1,500-ft limestone canyon walls; both the desert-transparent night sky and the canyon-wall glow ride on atmospheric state.

us-106-P02.name: Santa Elena Milky Way / star field
us-106-P02.description: Rio Grande-carved 1,500-ft limestone canyon walls; both the desert-transparent night sky and the canyon-wall glow ride on atmospheric state.

us-107-P01.name: Exit Glacier tongue and valley
us-107-P01.description: The Exit Glacier tongue spills from the Harding Icefield valley; terraced trails face the ice front and meltwater stream, and the ice banding only reads in low-angle light.

us-108-P01.name: Murphy Dome aurora over tundra
us-108-P01.description: A hilltop aurora lookout about 45 km northwest of Fairbanks with a 360-degree unobstructed horizon under the auroral oval; the contract decides the night window and cloud state, while actual aurora visibility is judged by the live aurora_state (NOAA OVATION) provider and stays fail-closed until that link is connected.

us-109-P01.name: Beluga Point sunset over Turnagain Arm
us-109-P01.description: A highway-side shore stop where the sun sets behind the Chugach ridge line across Turnagain Arm, with the exposed tidal flats catching low light; the bore tide is an occasional event and is deliberately not part of the evaluation criteria.

us-110-P01.name: Thompson Pass snow-wall panorama
us-110-P01.description: One of North America's snowiest mountain passes: the Richardson Highway crosses the ridge with snow walls persisting into late spring and stacked ridges running toward Worthington Glacier; the depth layering is decided by haze and low/mid cloud.

us-112-P01.name: Halemaʻumaʻu crater rim at night
us-112-P01.description: A night subject on the Kīlauea summit rim: the contract decides the night window and cloud state; whether the crater glows depends entirely on the eruption state (USGS HVO activity level). Until that state is connected the glow is honestly not_evaluatable and never fabricated from forecast data.

us-113-P01.name: Haleakalā summit sunrise above the cloud sea
us-113-P01.description: From the 3,055 m summit the sea of clouds catches the first dawn light; the sunrise window plus clear-over-cloud probabilities come from the forecast. Summit sunrise hours are reservation-only (Recreation.gov vehicle reservation) — the reservation is an entry gate, not a weather criterion.

us-114-P01.name: Kalalau Valley clouds and mist
us-114-P01.description: From the 4,000-ft rim the whole Kalalau Valley opens below; the deciding metrics are visibility and the push-and-pull of valley cloud — when the cloud is drawn out the green ridgelines and sea cliffs appear in full.

us-115-P01.name: Milky Way over Maunakea VIS
us-115-P01.description: The VIS parking lot at 2,804 m is the no-permit stargazing point (the observatory summit district needs 4WD and clearance): at 19.7°N the galactic core climbs high, and the moon criteria are strict.

us-116-P01.name: Waipiʻo Valley in morning light
us-116-P01.description: A rim view at the valley mouth: morning light separates the black-sand beach, waterfalls and green walls into layers. The valley access road has been closed to pedestrians since 2022 (Hawaiʻi DLNR); this subject evaluates only the outlook's shootability.

us-117-P01.name: Makapuʻu lighthouse sunrise seascape
us-117-P01.description: An east-facing lighthouse cliff: the sunrise window is drawn on the seaward sector, with the tower and cliffs silhouetted against first light; winter whale-watching (Nov–Mar) is a seasonal note, not an evaluation criterion.

us-118-P01.name: Pipeline sunset and wave light
us-118-P01.description: A world-class North Shore break: the sun drops to the northwest horizon and the wave faces turn translucent in low light. Big-wave events are a winter event state — this subject's criteria are the sunset window and cloud state, with swell height as an on-site hint only.

us-119-P01.name: Petrified dune waves of The Wave
us-119-P01.description: 200-million-year-old petrified dunes carved into swirling striations in Coyote Buttes North (BLM permitted area); disjoint from existing Arizona slots and Horseshoe Bend - here the petrified-dune waves.

us-120-P01.name: Rowena Crest gorge panorama
us-120-P01.description: From Rowena Crest the Columbia tears west through the Cascades as a transverse gorge (Friends of the Columbia Gorge; spring wildflowers and famous cleared views); disjoint from existing Portland-area gorge falls and Mt Rainier spots.

us-121-P01.name: Bixby Bridge at sunset
us-121-P01.description: The 1932 open-spandrel arch spans a sheer coastal canyon into the Pacific sunset - one of California's classic road compositions (Wikipedia; ~85 m deck); disjoint from us-122 McWay Falls (waterfall subject) 14 km south.

us-121-P02.name: Bixby Bridge moonlit coast
us-121-P02.description: A moonlit coast around full moon: the Bixby Creek bridge and coastline under raking moonlight - bridge shadow and wave edges (moon elevation 5-30 deg); needs illumination >= 85%, total cloud <= 30% and no rain; coast semantics.

us-122-P01.name: McWay Falls onto the beach
us-122-P01.description: One of the few US waterfalls dropping directly onto a beach (California State Parks; overlook-only, beach closed); disjoint from the Bixby Bridge arch subject 14 km north.

us-123-P01.name: Maroon Bells lake mirror
us-123-P01.description: One of the most photographed mountain scenes in North America: twin maroon peaks mirrored in Maroon Lake on windless mornings (USFS); disjoint from existing Colorado spots.

us-124-P01.name: Keystone Canyon twin falls
us-124-P01.description: The Richardson-cut gorge near Valdez with Bridal Veil and Horsetail falls on the walls, frozen into icefalls in winter (Wikipedia); disjoint from inland Denali mountain scenery.

us-125-P01.name: Kancamagus foliage corridor
us-125-P01.description: A scenic national-forest highway without services, foliage blazing along the Swift River (USFS; typical peak late Sep-late Oct); disjoint from coastal Acadia, Maine.

us-126-P01.name: Linn Cove Viaduct in fall color
us-126-P01.description: The S-shaped steel viaduct wraps the Grandfather Mountain ridgeline in autumn color (NPS; typical peak mid-Oct-early Nov); disjoint from other Appalachian points.

us-127-P01.name: White Pocket cauliflower rock
us-127-P01.description: Swirled Navajo sandstone 'cauliflower' domes under white caps (BLM; no trails, free-roam, deep-sand 4WD access - access not scored); 12 km from the permitted Wave (us-119) but a different landform and no lottery.

us-128-P01.name: Reflection Canyon S-bend
us-128-P01.description: The Navajo sandstone S-bend above Lake Powell in Glen Canyon NRA (NPS; route-finding over ~16-18 miles with no trail, coordinates are the overlook estimate - access not scored, honestly labeled); disjoint from existing Arizona canyon subjects.

us-129-P01.name: Factory Butte badland moonscape
us-129-P01.description: Silver-gray Mancos Shale badlands scoured into a lunar plain with the lone butte rising (Wikipedia/recreation.gov; SR-24 west of Hanksville; lithology verified 2026-11-10 via americansouthwest.net/utah/factory-butte - Upper Blue Hills are Mancos Shale, butte tops Emery sandstone); disjoint from White Pocket's colored swirls.

us-130-P01.name: Coal Mine Canyon rim stripes
us-130-P01.description: Red-and-white striped badlands seen from the rim (thewave.info; the rim is Navajo Nation land requiring a permit and the interior is Hopi with guide-required access - access not scored, honestly labeled); disjoint from the petrified-dune subjects of us-119/129.

us-131-P01.name: Bisti hoodoos and petrified wood
us-131-P01.description: Mushroom hoodoos, winged rocks and petrified wood in layered mudstone (BLM wilderness; no trails, sparse navigation - access not scored); disjoint from Factory Butte's broad gray plain.

us-132-P01.name: Bonsai Rock over still water
us-132-P01.description: A granite turret crowned with junipers 'bonsai', mirrored on calm water (Nevada east shore; steep boulder descent - access not scored); disjoint from existing California lake subjects.

us-133-P01.name: Ancient bristlecone twisted trunks
us-133-P01.description: Twisted ancients near 5,000 years old on the White Mountains at 3,000 m (USFS; seasonal winter road closure - access not scored); disjoint from the Mono Lake east-slope spot us-100.

us-134-P01.name: Apostle Islands icicle caves
us-134-P01.description: The ice-cave route opens only when Lake Superior ice is thick enough (typically Jan-Mar, dates yearly announced by NPS) - the window tracks the official opening, never a guarantee; disjoint from the Niagara subject.

us-135-P01.name: Caddo cypress bayou
us-135-P01.description: Centuries-old bald cypress draped with Spanish moss in still bayous with morning fog (Wikipedia; best by boat - informational access note); disjoint from the existing Midwest plains subject.

us-136-P01.name: Palo Duro Lighthouse
us-136-P01.description: Red-and-orange walls with the capped Lighthouse spire (TPWD state park; a ~20-mile canyon on the plains); geographically far from the Grand Canyon with no 5 km conflict - a plain-ringed red canyon.

us-137-P01.name: Watkins Glen gorge cascades
us-137-P01.description: Nineteen waterfalls and arched bridges in a 400-ft carved gorge (NY State Parks; winter trail closure - access informational); disjoint from other Eastern US subjects.

us-138-P01.name: Sparks Lane morning fog
us-138-P01.description: A split-rail fence lane across a farm cove in morning fog (NPS Cades Cove; elk and deer sightings common); disjoint from other Eastern US subjects.

us-139-P01.name: Crystal Mill in autumn
us-139-P01.description: An 1892 wooden powerhouse perched on Crystal River boulders, boxed in by golden aspen (NRHP-listed; private rough road - access informational); disjoint from other Colorado subjects.

us-140-P01.name: Ice Lake turquoise mirror
us-140-P01.description: A 3,735 m cirque lake mirroring 13,000-ft walls, mineral-turquoise water (USFS; ~8 mi trail with 2,900 ft gain - access not scored); disjoint from us-123 Maroon Bells.

us-141-P01.name: Last Dollar Road aspen valley
us-141-P01.description: A dirt ridgeline over the aspen valley below Wilson Peak and the Telluride basin (Telluride tourism; typical peak late Sep-mid Oct); disjoint from the mill subject us-142.

us-142-P01.name: Great Sand Dunes and snow ranges
us-142-P01.description: The tallest dunes in North America (to ~750 ft) stacked against the snow-capped Sangre de Cristos (NPS; spring Medano Creek surge is informational); disjoint from White Sands' gypsum dunes.

us-143-P01.name: Trillium Lake Hood mirror
us-143-P01.description: A glacial tarn mirroring Mount Hood's glacier (USFS; winter ice-and-snow lake); disjoint from the Washington Cascades spots.

us-144-P01.name: Abiqua Falls basalt amphitheater
us-144-P01.description: A 92-ft fall over columnar basalt into an amphitheater plunge pool (private road walk-in - access informational); disjoint from Proxy Falls' forest-cascade subject.

us-145-P01.name: Proxy Falls twin cascade
us-145-P01.description: Twin cascades over mossy basalt at the edge of the Three Sisters Wilderness (USFS; easy 1.6-mile loop); disjoint from Abiqua's basalt amphitheater.

us-146-P01.name: Painted Hills banded hills
us-146-P01.description: Miocene volcanic-ash paleosols banded red, orange, gold and black (NPS; bands are richest after rain - informational); disjoint from other Oregon/Washington spots.

us-147-P01.name: Zebra Slot striped walls
us-147-P01.description: Orange-and-white stripes like zebra hide in an arm-width slot (Escalante; a wading pool section - access informational); kin to Zion Narrows/Antelope but a different stripe pattern and scale.

us-148-P01.name: Bentonite banded hills
us-148-P01.description: Volcanic-ash clay banded brown, red, purple, gray and green into soft domes (NPS; impassable clay roads after rain and footprint-recovery bans - access not scored); disjoint from Painted Hills' fossil-bed bands.

us-149-P01.name: Joshua Tree Milky Way night
us-149-P01.description: A certified dark-sky park: night sky over Joshua tree silhouettes on the Mojave-M Colorado junction (NPS; spring bloom is P02); disjoint from the Owens Valley dark-sky spot.

us-149-P02.name: Joshua tree bloom
us-149-P02.description: Unusual spring blossoms (NPS; bloom timing floats with winter rains); same park as P01, different season.

us-150-P01.name: Trona tufa spires
us-150-P01.description: More than 500 tufa towers rising from a dry Pleistocene lakebed (BLM; a 3.5-mile dirt road - access informational); kin to Mono Lake tufa but dry-land towers, a different form.

us-151-P01.name: Painted Dunes and Cinder Cone
us-151-P01.description: Oxidized volcanic-ash bands beside the Cinder Cone crater (NPS; Butte Lake district summer access - informational); disjoint from the Lassen hot-spring subject.

us-152-P01.name: Alice Lake Sawtooth mirror
us-152-P01.description: A 2,622 m cirque lake mirroring El Capitan in the Sawtooths (lakes can stay frozen into early summer - informational; within the Idaho Central Dark Sky Reserve, night sky a bonus); geographically disjoint from the Great Basin/Arizona dark-sky spots.

us-153-P01.name: Craters of the Moon night sky
us-153-P01.description: An International Dark Sky Park over basalt lava fields - lava domes and lava tubes by day, Milky Way by night (NPS); disjoint from us-152's lake-mirror subject.

us-154-P01.name: Shoshone Falls spring surge
us-154-P01.description: A 212-ft fault drop of the Snake River, higher than Niagara, at spring peak before irrigation diversions (City of Twin Falls; summer flows drop - informational); disjoint from the Utah falls subjects (us-144/145).

us-155-P01.name: Fort Jefferson sunset
us-155-P01.description: A giant brick fort on a Gulf-of-Mexico coral island (NPS; ferry/seaplane only - access informational); disjoint from Acadia and the Florida mainland subjects.

us-156-P01.name: Cape Hatteras striped light
us-156-P01.description: America's tallest brick lighthouse (198 ft) with its black-white spiral bands on the Outer Banks (NPS); disjoint from the inland viaduct subject us-126.

us-157-P01.name: Assateague horses at dawn beach
us-157-P01.description: The famous wild horses roaming a dawn beach and salt marsh on the Atlantic barrier island (NPS; viewing distance and insect season informational); disjoint from other Eastern subjects.

us-158-P01.name: Harding Icefield panorama
us-158-P01.description: The 8.2-mile trail's top looks over the 700-square-mile icefield and its outlet glaciers (NPS; summer trail - access not scored); disjoint from inland Denali scenery and the Keystone falls.

us-159-P01.name: Old Faithful eruption column
us-159-P01.description: The world's most famous predictable cone geyser, columns 30-55 m (NPS; eruption intervals are published on-site by park staff at the Visitor Center/NPS App - an access note, NOT a forecast contract; steam reads best on cold early mornings); disjoint from the Grand Prismatic colored-pool subject.

us-160-P01.name: Morning Glory Pool color rings
us-160-P01.description: Deep blue core ringed by orange bacterial mats (Wikipedia/NPS; boardwalk-only, no off-trail entry - access not scored; midday top-light is the color optimum, opposite of golden hour - recorded honestly); kin to Grand Prismatic 5.4 km away but a small concentric-ring scale.

us-161-P01.name: Halemaʻumaʻu lava-glow night
us-161-P01.description: Lava-lake glow lighting the plume above Halemaʻumaʻu from the rim overlook, governed by USGS HVO activity state; long exposure; SO2/vog downwind caution - safety note; the park is open 24 h but rim areas may close during eruptive episodes - access follows on-site notices; disjoint from us-112's Milky-Way night-sky subject (glow there is honestly not_evaluatable) - here the lava glow itself, with a NEW REQUIRED volcanic_activity condition tied to USGS HVO status.

us-162-P01.name: Nāhuku lava-tube interior
us-162-P01.description: A giant lava tube beneath 500-year-old rainforest (NPS; the tube is lit 08:00-20:00, bring a flashlight outside those hours - access informational; disjoint from the glow-night and night-sky subjects - here the tube geology.)

us-163-P01.name: Kīlauea Iki lava-lake floor
us-163-P01.description: The solidified 1959 lava-lake floor with steaming fissures (NPS; a 4-mile loop - trail distance not scored; midday top-light shows surface texture best - honestly recorded; disjoint from the underground-tube subject of Nāhuku.)
